ticket.title: a contract change compiles in its own repo and breaks consumers in two others, and no gate builds across repositories
ticket.description: Measured 2026-11-10, and it has already cost ten tickets. SP-41 added three optional fields to VerificationReceipt in gaugeblock-contracts. Every storypole gate ran green, because storypole own workspace compiled. Two consumers construct that type literally and do not spread defaults: joiner-core src/engine/mod.rs and benchwork-core tests/archive_service_tests.rs. Both stopped compiling the moment the contract landed. Nothing reported it - no chain builds across repositories, and miter contracts checks schema drift rather than compilation - so the breakage sat in main until an unrelated storypole verification happened to pull joiner-core into its build, and then benchwork into another. Two fix commits later (joiner a301233, benchwork de8ad04) main compiles again. OF-41 is the sibling gate and deliberately does not cover this: it resolves every member from outside the suite with cargo metadata, which answers published-crates-only, and it never compiles. Wanted: a cross-repository build check - each member compiled against the workspace as checked out, in one pass, failing with the crate and the diagnostic - run at the atomic-commit gate for any change to a shared contract crate. Acceptance: reverting SP-41 contract change makes the gate fail naming joiner-core and benchwork-core, restoring it makes the gate pass, and a change confined to one repository does not pay for the whole fleet.
